ST.EMPTY: Load a program (Ctrl+F9) and run it to see its statistics.

KPI.HELP: Each instruction that goes through the ID stage counts as executed. In an ideal 5-stage pipeline the CPI gets close to 1: each stall cycle moves it away.

CYCLES.TITLE: Where do the cycles go?
CYCLES.MAIN_CAUSE: The pipeline stops most because of {{cause}}: {{per}} % of the cycles. The «Stalls» tab explains how to reduce them.
CYCLES.NO_STALLS: There are no stalls: the pipeline moves on in every cycle.

STALL.INTRO: {{total}} stall cycles ({{per}} % of the cycles). A stall is a cycle in which an instruction cannot move on to its next stage.

RAW.NAME: RAW stalls (data dependencies)
RAW.HELP: An instruction needs a result that another one has not computed yet (read after write). Forwarding avoids many of them; moving the instruction that uses the value away from the one that produces it avoids the rest.

WAW.NAME: WAW stalls
WAW.HELP: An instruction would write a register before an older one that writes the same register (write after write). It happens with multi-cycle floating point units: use another destination register.

STRUCTURAL.NAME: structural stalls
STRUCTURAL.HELP: Two instructions want the same functional unit, or to write in WB at the same time. More floating point units in the configuration, or spreading the operations, reduce them.

CONTROL.NAME: control stalls
CONTROL.HELP: Each taken branch throws away the instruction fetched after it (the pipeline predicts not taken). Fewer taken branches (for example, unrolling loops) reduce them.

TRAP.NAME: trap stalls
TRAP.HELP: A trap waits for the older instructions to finish before talking to the outside (input, output or the end of the program).

RAW.TITLE: Why do the data wait? (RAW stalls)

LOAD.NAME: After a load
LOAD.HELP: An instruction uses the value of a load right after it: the value arrives in MEM, one cycle late even with forwarding. Put another instruction between them.

BRANCH.NAME: In a branch
BRANCH.HELP: The branch is resolved in ID and needs its register there, before the previous instruction computes it in EX.

FLOATING.NAME: From a multi-cycle operation
FLOATING.HELP: The value comes from a floating point addition, multiplication or division, or from an integer multiplication or division, which in DLX use the same units and take several cycles.

OTHER.NAME: Others
OTHER.HELP: The rest of the dependencies between integer instructions (without forwarding, almost all of them).

BRANCHES.TITLE: Conditional branches
BRANCHES.HELP: The pipeline predicts that branches are not taken: each taken branch costs a control stall cycle.
BRANCHES.NONE: The program has not executed conditional branches.

FLOATING.TITLE: Operations in the floating point units
FLOATING.NONE: The program has not executed floating point operations.
FLOATING.HELP: In DLX, the integer multiplication and division (mult, multu, div, divu) also use these units and count here.

COMPARE.HELP: Runs the program to the end with both options (and the rest of the configuration) and shows the difference.
COMPARE.FAILED: It could not be compared: load a program without errors.

COMPARE.STOPPED_ERROR: One of the runs ended with an error: {{error}}

MACHINE.CYCLE_CLOCK_DIAGRAM_KEYS: Cycle clock diagram. With the focus, the arrows move it, + and - zoom it, 0 goes back to the initial size, Home goes to the start and End to the last cycle.
MACHINE.DIAGRAM_HELP_TITLE: How to move around the diagram
MACHINE.DIAGRAM_HELP_1: Drag the diagram with the mouse or a finger; two fingers, or Ctrl and the wheel, zoom it.
MACHINE.DIAGRAM_HELP_2: Click the diagram to give it the focus: then the arrows (or J, L, I, K) move it.
MACHINE.DIAGRAM_HELP_3: + and - zoom in and out, and 0 goes back to the initial size.
MACHINE.DIAGRAM_HELP_4: Home (or R) goes to the first cycle and the top of the table; End goes to the last cycle.
MACHINE.DIAGRAM_HELP_5: The diagram follows the last cycle until you move back, and follows it again when you reach the end.
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_RAW: {{label}} in cycle {{cycle}}: {{instruction}} needs {{register}}, which {{cause}} computes, and does not have it yet (data hazard, read after write).
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_RAW_REAL: Forwarding is on: it is a real dependency, the value is not computed yet (for example, a load followed by its use).
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_RAW_FORWARDING_HELPS: With forwarding it would not have stalled in this cycle: the value was already computed, but without forwarding it must wait until it is written in the register (WB).
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_RAW_NOT_YET: In this cycle the value is not computed yet, so it would wait with forwarding too.
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_WAW: {{label}} in cycle {{cycle}}: {{instruction}} writes {{register}}, as {{cause}} does, which is still executing; it waits so as not to write before it (write after write hazard).
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_STRUCTURAL: {{label}} in cycle {{cycle}}: there is no free floating point unit for {{instruction}} (structural hazard). With more units in the configuration it would not wait.
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_MEM: {{label}} in cycle {{cycle}}: {{cause}} uses the MEM stage in this cycle, so {{instruction}} waits for its turn (the floating point units go first).
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_TRAP: {{label}} in cycle {{cycle}}: {{instruction}} is a trap and waits in IF until the pipeline is empty.
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_INPUT: {{label}} in cycle {{cycle}}: {{instruction}} waits for a line of the console.
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_BLOCKED: {{label}} in cycle {{cycle}}: {{instruction}} waits behind {{cause}}, which is stalled.
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_ABORTED: Aborted in cycle {{cycle}}: {{instruction}} had been fetched after {{cause}}, which jumps (branches are predicted not taken) or ends the program.
MACHINE.EXPLAIN_HELP: Click a cell of the diagram, or use the buttons, to see why an instruction stalls.
MACHINE.NO_STALLS: There are no stalls in the diagram.
MACHINE.TABLE_CAPTION: The last {{count}} cycles: the stage or the stall of each instruction in each cycle
MACHINE.GO_TO_START: Go to the start of the program ({{address}}): it has no main label
MACHINE.DESCRIPTION_HINT: Press the description of an instruction to see what it does, the fields of its code and what happens in each stage of the pipeline.
MACHINE.DIAGRAM_EMPTY: Load a program and step through its cycles to see how its instructions go through the pipeline.
MACHINE.MEMORY_WRITTEN: Word written in the last cycle
MACHINE.MEMORY_READ: Word read in the last cycle

CONFIG.HELP_FORWARDING: An instruction gets the result of the previous one as soon as it is computed, without waiting for it to be written in the registers. Without forwarding, each data dependency costs up to two more cycles (R-Stall).
CONFIG.HELP_FLOATING_POINT: How many units of each kind there are and how many cycles each operation takes in them. The units are not pipelined: with only one, a second operation waits for the first to finish (S-Stall).
CONFIG.HELP_MEMORY_SIZE: In bytes, from 512 to 1,048,576 and a multiple of 8. The code starts at 0x100 and the data at 0x1000.
CONFIG.HELP_TIME_SIMULATION: When running (F9), the pause between a cycle and the next one. With 0, as fast as possible.
CONFIG.HELP_AUTO_SAVE: When leaving the editor, saves the file and its breakpoints. Without it, the unsaved changes and the breakpoints are lost.
CONFIG.HELP_MULTIVIEW: Which windows the multiview shows and in which column. They are dragged by their handle.
CONFIG.CONFIRM_MESSAGE: The new configuration loads the program into the simulator again and the simulation going on is lost.
CONFIG.DIAGRAM_HISTORY: History of the cycle clock diagram (cycles)
CONFIG.HELP_DIAGRAM_HISTORY: How many cycles the diagram keeps, from 100 to 100,000; the oldest ones go. A long history makes long programs use more memory.
CONFIG.LOCKED_BY_EXERCISE: This program is a shared exercise: some options are locked and those of the exercise are used.
CONFIG.HELP_ARCHITECTURE: The machine THUMDER simulates. It can also be chosen in the header. Programs end the same in both: only the cycles change.

SUPERDLX.TITLE: SuperDLX
SUPERDLX.HELP: The parameters of the MACHINE file of WinSuperDLX: how many instructions go through per cycle, the size of each structure and the functional units.
SUPERDLX.HELP_WIDTHS: How many instructions are fetched, decoded (sent to their window and to the ROB) and committed each cycle, from 1 to 16.
SUPERDLX.HELP_STRUCTURES: The entries of each structure: when one is full, the stage that fills it stops.
SUPERDLX.HELP_PREDICTION: Without it, fetch stops at each branch until it is resolved.

ITABLE.INTRO: The {{count}} instructions that THUMDER assembles and simulates, taken from the definitions of its engine. Search for one or filter by type, and tap one to see its syntax, what it does, the fields of its 32-bit word and what happens in each stage of the pipeline.
ITABLE.CLEAR: Clear the search and the filter

CATEGORY_HELP.ALU: They add, subtract, multiply, divide or combine bit by bit two registers, or a register and a 16-bit immediate.
CATEGORY_HELP.COMPARE: They compare two integers and leave 1 or 0 in a register; followed by BEQZ or BNEZ, they make a conditional jump.
CATEGORY_HELP.SHIFT: They move the bits of a register left or right: logical (zeros come in) or arithmetic (the sign is copied).
CATEGORY_HELP.MEMORY: The only ones that use memory (in MEM): they read or write a byte, a half word, a word or a floating point number at the address base + displacement.
CATEGORY_HELP.CONTROL: They change the PC. They are decided in ID, and THUMDER predicts not taken: if the jump is taken, the instruction already fetched is aborted. JAL and JALR save the return address in R31.
CATEGORY_HELP.FLOAT: They work on the F registers in single or double precision (IEEE 754), in the floating point units, which take several cycles; the comparisons leave their result in FPSR.
CATEGORY_HELP.CONVERT: They change the type of a number (integer, single or double precision) inside the F registers.
CATEGORY_HELP.MOVE: They copy registers: between F registers, or between the integer and the floating point ones, without converting their bits.
CATEGORY_HELP.OTHER: The system calls (TRAP: end, read, write, printf…), NOP and RFE.

ITABLE.DOUBLES: A double register is a pair: F0 names F0:F1, so its number has to be even.

UNITS.FADD: faddEX, the floating point addition unit (the cycles of the configuration)
UNITS.FMUL: fmultEX, the multiplication unit (the cycles of the configuration)
UNITS.FDIV: fdivEX, the division unit (the cycles of the configuration)

ITABLE.MAP_OPCODE_HELP: The I and J type instructions. The codes 0x00 and 0x01 are the R and F types, whose operation is in the function code.
ITABLE.MAP_R_HELP: With opcode 0x00 (SPECIAL): the operations between integer registers.
ITABLE.MAP_F_HELP: With opcode 0x01 (FPARITH): the floating point operations.
ITABLE.MAP_CORNER_OPCODE: Rows: bits 31 to 29; columns: bits 28 to 26
ITABLE.MAP_CORNER_FUNC: Rows: bits 5 to 3; columns: bits 2 to 0
ITABLE.MAP_OPENS_R: see the function codes of the R type

CONSENT.MESSAGE: THUMDER keeps in your browser what it needs to work: your files, the settings and the language. With your permission, it also counts the visits with Google Analytics, which uses cookies, and sends technical reports when something fails so that it can be fixed.
CONSENT.SETTINGS_INTRO: Choose what you allow THUMDER to do. You can change it whenever you want from "Privacy settings", in the footer.

CONSENT.ANALYTICS_HELP: Google Analytics for Firebase counts, in aggregate, the visits and the views used, to know what to improve. It uses the cookies _ga and _ga_<id> (up to 2 years) and Google may process the data in the United States.

SOUND.NAME: Sound
SOUND.HELP: The simulation sounds: each stage of the pipeline has its note, and the stalls, the taken branches and the events have their own sound. You can hear how the program goes on without looking.
SOUND.STAGES: A note for each stage an instruction enters
SOUND.STAGES_HELP: Without it only the events sound: program loaded, errors, breakpoint, console input and end of the program. When the cycles go very fast, one in a few sounds.
SOUND.LEGEND_STAGES: Stages: IF sounds G, ID C, EX E, MEM G and WB a high C with a little bell when the instruction ends; the floating point units, A, D and a high A. With the pipeline full, each cycle is a chord from low to high.
SOUND.LEGEND_PROBLEMS: Problems: a stalled instruction sounds like a dull knock, and one aborted by a taken branch, like something falling.
SOUND.LEGEND_EVENTS: Events: three notes going up when loading, two clashing notes if there are errors, two bells at a breakpoint, a question when the program waits for a line and a chord at the end.
SOUND.NOW: The changes of the sound are saved at once; it is also turned on and off from the menu of the speed in the navbar.

STAGES.TITLE: What each stage does in cycle {{cycle}}
STAGES.TAKEN: taken: the instruction in IF is aborted
STAGES.FORWARDED: Forwarding from {{from}} to {{to}}: the value arrives without waiting for it to be written in the register.

EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_PC: Program counter: the address of the next instruction to fetch in IF. Changing it makes the fetch go on at that address (the instructions already in the pipeline carry on).
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_IMAR: The address of the instruction just fetched in IF (instruction memory address register).
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_IR: The instruction just fetched in IF, encoded in 32 bits (instruction register); it is decoded in ID.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_A: The first operand the instruction reads from the register file in ID.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_AHI: The high half of A, for 64-bit operands.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_B: The second operand the instruction reads from the register file in ID.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_BHI: The high half of B, for 64-bit operands.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_BTA: The target address of the last jump or branch (branch target address).
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_ALU: The result of the last operation of the EX stage.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_ALUHI: The second word of a 64-bit (double) result of EX.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_FPSR: Floating point status: its bit 0 is the result of the last comparison (EQF, LTD…), the one BFPT and BFPF read. The simulator only keeps that bit.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_DMAR: The address of the last data read or written in memory in MEM (data memory address register).
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_SDR: The data of the last store, the one written to memory.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_SDRHI: The second word of the data of a 64-bit store.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_LDR: The data of the last load, read from memory.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_LDRHI: The second word of the data of a 64-bit load.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_INTEGER: A 32-bit integer. Signed, it is read in two's complement: bit 31 is the sign.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_R31: A 32-bit integer. JAL and JALR store the return address in R31.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_FLOAT: A single precision floating point number (IEEE 754, 32 bits): sign, 8 bits of exponent and 23 of fraction.
EDIT_REGISTER.HELP_DOUBLE: A double precision number (IEEE 754, 64 bits) takes two registers: {{high}} keeps the high 32 bits and {{low}} the low 32.
EDIT_REGISTER.LOCKED_R0: R0 is always 0 in DLX: whatever is written to it is discarded. Choose another register to edit it.
EDIT_REGISTER.LOCKED_LATCH: {{name}} is written by the pipeline every cycle: its value is shown here, but the simulator does not let it change. Of the control registers, PC and FPSR can be edited.

EDIT_VALUE.INVALID_HEX: Type up to {{digits}} hexadecimal digits (0-9, A-F).
EDIT_VALUE.INVALID_NUMBER: Type a number: 3.14, -0.5, 1e-3, Infinity or NaN.
EDIT_VALUE.ROUNDED: {{text}} does not fit exactly in {{bits}} bits: the nearest one is kept, {{exact}}.
EDIT_VALUE.BITS_HELP: Click a bit to flip it. With the keyboard: the arrows go from bit to bit and Space flips it.
EDIT_VALUE.REPRESENTATIONS: The new value in each representation
EDIT_VALUE.STATUS_ADJUSTED: The simulator adjusted it when storing it: {{name}} = {{value}}.
EDIT_VALUE.STATUS_REJECTED: The simulator did not accept it (is a program loaded?): {{name}} = {{value}} is only shown in the tables.
EDIT_VALUE.NO_PROGRAM: No program is loaded: the simulator will not keep the changes.
EDIT_VALUE.APPLY_HINT: Apply (or Enter) stores the value in the simulator; the dialog stays open.

EDIT_MEMORY.SIZE: {{bytes}} bytes ({{bits}} bits), at an address multiple of {{align}}.
EDIT_MEMORY.SIZE_DOUBLE: 8 bytes (64 bits): two words in a row, at an address multiple of 4.
EDIT_MEMORY.ARROWS_HELP: The arrows ↑ ↓ go to the previous and the next item.
EDIT_MEMORY.INVALID_ADDRESS: Type an address in hexadecimal, up to 8 digits.
EDIT_MEMORY.MISALIGNED: An item of {{bytes}} bytes starts at an address multiple of {{align}}. Try:
EDIT_MEMORY.OUT_OF_MEMORY: Out of memory: it has {{size}} bytes, and the last item of this type starts at {{last}}.
EDIT_MEMORY.INSTRUCTION: The code of {{instruction}} is here: changing this word changes the program.
EDIT_MEMORY.GRID_HELP: DLX is big-endian: the byte at the lowest address is the most significant.

LOG.RESET: The program of the editor is loaded in the simulator («Load» button): the machine is emptied first.
LOG.CLEAR: The machine is reset: memory, code and registers to zero, with no program loaded.
LOG.INIT: The simulator assembles the program, puts the code and the data in the memory and leaves the machine in cycle 0.
LOG.STEP: Cycle {{cycle}} simulated: the instruction fetched is the one of line {{line}} of the editor.
LOG.STEP_NO_LINE: Cycle {{cycle}} simulated: the instruction fetched is not in the file of the editor (it is in a module, such as input.s), or none was fetched because the pipeline waits.
LOG.CONFIG: The configuration is sent to the simulator.
LOG.CONFIG_FORWARDING: Configuration sent to the simulator: with forwarding, {{memory}} bytes of memory; units × cycles: fadd {{fadd}}, fmul {{fmul}}, fdiv {{fdiv}}.
LOG.CONFIG_NO_FORWARDING: Configuration sent to the simulator: without forwarding, {{memory}} bytes of memory; units × cycles: fadd {{fadd}}, fmul {{fmul}}, fdiv {{fdiv}}.
LOG.TAGS: The editor read the labels of the program: {{count}}.

ARCH.TITLE: Architecture
ARCH.DLX_SUMMARY: The five-stage pipeline of WinDLX: one instruction per cycle, in order.
ARCH.SUPERDLX_SUMMARY: Superscalar with out of order execution, as WinSuperDLX: several instructions per cycle, windows, ROB and branch prediction.
ARCH.CHANGED: {{name}} is simulated now: the program has been loaded again.
ARCH.LOCKED: The exercise open locks the architecture.
ARCH.RELOADS: Changing it loads the program again in the other machine.

SUPERSCALAR.TITLE: Superscalar machine
SUPERSCALAR.EMPTY: Load a program without errors to see the SuperDLX machine.
SUPERSCALAR.EMPTY_READY: Run one cycle (F8) to see the SuperDLX machine.
SUPERSCALAR.MACHINE_SUMMARY: It fetches {{fetch}}, decodes {{decode}} and commits {{commit}} instructions per cycle, with ROBs of {{robInt}} and {{robFp}} entries and windows of {{windowInt}} and {{windowFp}}.

FETCH_STOP.queueFull: Fetch stopped: the queue is full
FETCH_STOP.branch: Fetch stopped: waits for a branch (no prediction)
FETCH_STOP.jreg: Fetch stopped: waits for the register of a jr or jalr
FETCH_STOP.halt: Fetch stopped: trap 0, the program ends
FETCH_STOP.fault: Fetch stopped: address out of memory
FETCH_STOP.recovery: Fetch stopped: recovering from a misprediction

SUPERSCALAR.HEAD: head
SUPERSCALAR.RENAME_HELP: Which instruction of the ROB will write each register: the ones that read it wait for that instruction, not for the register.

CELL.D: Decoded: goes to its window and to the ROB
CELL.w: Waits in the window for its operands or a unit
CELL.r: Waits in the ROB to commit

DIAGRAM.EMPTY: Run the simulation to see the cycles.
DIAGRAM.CAPTION: Cycles {{first}} to {{last}}
DIAGRAM.CUT: The last instructions are shown: {{count}} more do not fit.
DIAGRAM.MISPREDICTED: Mispredicted branch: what was fetched after it was squashed
DIAGRAM.RETIRED: NOP or J: it is resolved in fetch and only waits to commit.
DIAGRAM.SPAN_UNIT: {{cycles}} cycle(s) in its unit and in memory
DIAGRAM.IN_FLIGHT: It is still in the machine.
DIAGRAM.CHOOSE: Choose an instruction to see how long it waited in each place.
DIAGRAM.HELP_1: Each row is an instruction, in the order it was fetched (#n); each column, a cycle.
DIAGRAM.HELP_2: An instruction goes through the queue (q), its window (w), its unit (E), the memory (M) and the ROB (r) until it commits (C).
DIAGRAM.HELP_3: Instructions start out of order, as soon as they have their operands and a unit, but they commit in order.
DIAGRAM.HELP_4: A mispredicted branch squashes (X) everything fetched after it; the table of events gives the cycle of each step of every instruction.

KPI.HELP: IPC: instructions committed per cycle, at most {{peak}} of each half (integer and floating point). The squashed ones are those fetched after a mispredicted branch.

COMMITS.TITLE: Cycles by the instructions they commit
COMMITS.HELP: How many cycles committed 0, 1, 2... instructions. The cycles with 0 are the ones to reduce.

STALLS.INTRO: The cycles in which a stage did nothing, and why. A stage that stops leaves the next ones without work.

queueFull.NAME: Queue full
queueFull.HELP: Decode cannot keep up: the windows, the ROBs or the buffers are full.

branch.NAME: Waits for a branch
branch.HELP: Without prediction, fetch waits until each branch is resolved.

jreg.NAME: Waits for jr or jalr
jreg.HELP: A jump to a register: fetch waits until the register is known.

recovery.NAME: Recovery
recovery.HELP: The cycle lost after a misprediction, while what was fetched after the branch is squashed.

halt.NAME: End of the program
halt.HELP: After trap 0 is fetched nothing else is.

fault.NAME: Out of memory
fault.HELP: The fetch address is not in memory.

queueEmpty.NAME: Queue empty
queueEmpty.HELP: Fetch brings no instructions: branches, mispredictions or the end of the program.

robInt.NAME: Integer ROB full
robInt.HELP: Integer instructions do not commit in time: a slow one at the head holds all the ones behind it.

robFp.NAME: Floating point ROB full
robFp.HELP: Floating point instructions do not commit in time: a division or a multiplication at the head holds the others.

windowInt.NAME: Integer window full
windowInt.HELP: Too many integer instructions wait for their operands or for a unit.

windowFp.NAME: Floating point window full
windowFp.HELP: Too many floating point instructions wait for their operands or for a unit.

loadBuffer.NAME: Load buffer full
loadBuffer.HELP: Many loads wait for the memory or for older stores.

storeBuffer.NAME: Store buffer full
storeBuffer.HELP: Stores are written after they commit: they wait long in the buffer.

notDone.NAME: The head has not finished
notDone.HELP: The oldest instruction waits for its operands, its unit or the memory: the ones behind it wait with it (commit in order).

order.NAME: Waits for the other half
order.HELP: There is an older unresolved branch, trap or error in the other ROB.

storeData.NAME: Store without data
storeData.HELP: A store reaches the head without the data it writes.

trap.NAME: Trap
trap.HELP: A trap runs when it is the oldest instruction and the older stores are in memory.

input.NAME: Waits for input
input.HELP: Trap 3 waits for a line in the console.

WAITS.TITLE: Waits in the windows
WAITS.HELP: Each cycle an instruction spent in its window without starting: for its operands (data dependences) or because there was no free unit (structural hazard).
WAITS.LOADS: {{blocked}} of {{loads}} loads waited for an older store that could write the same bytes.

BRANCHES.OFF: Prediction is off: fetch stops at each branch and nothing is squashed.
BRANCHES.HELP: The BTB predicts in fetch with a 2-bit counter per branch; a branch that is not in it is predicted taken. Branches are resolved when they start in their unit.
BRANCHES.ALL_RIGHT: The predictor got every branch right.
BRANCHES.COST: The {{mispredicted}} mispredictions squashed {{squashed}} instructions fetched on the wrong path.

UNITS.HELP: Each unit is busy with an instruction for its whole latency (they are not pipelined). A high use with waits for a unit asks for more units of that kind.

OCCUPANCY.TITLE: Mean occupation
OCCUPANCY.HELP: How many entries each structure had busy on average. The one that is always full is the one that limits.

COMPARE.HELP: The same program to the end in DLX (with the configuration of its pipeline) and in SuperDLX (with its own).
COMPARE.SPEEDUP: SuperDLX is {{times}} times faster: {{superdlx}} cycles against {{dlx}} of DLX.
